project: E2 Structured JSON Worker Result Channel
description: Add an event-first, schema-validated JSON result channel for workstations so validated worker output is stored as native structuredResult data on resulting Work, survives replay, is available to downstream prompt templates and Work list/watch output, and fails through a stable typed dispatch failure when invalid.

context.customerAsk: Provide an optional JSON result contract per workstation, authored as JSON Schema in workstation configuration. Require and validate a JSON final response when configured, persist the validated payload on Work, expose it to downstream prompt templates and you work list/watch, and route schema violations as typed dispatch failures. Prove schema-pass templating and schema-violation failure routing with functional tests.
context.problem: The existing outputSchema path can validate raw model output but discards the parsed JSON value. Later stages still parse artifacts or text, replay and Work reads cannot reproduce the structured handoff, operators cannot inspect it through Work commands, and schema failures are not distinguishable from unrelated generic failures.
context.solution: Reuse outputSchema as the optional authoring contract, validate and detach the worker's final JSON value at the Workers boundary, carry native structuredResult data through canonical dispatch events and resulting Work projections, rebuild it through recordings/replay, expose it at .Inputs[n].StructuredResult and in Work CLI/API output, and classify malformed or schema-invalid responses as terminal structured_output_schema_violation failures that follow normal onFailure routing.

acceptanceCriteria: A workstation with a valid outputSchema accepts only a JSON final response satisfying that schema and records the validated value as native structuredResult data; a workstation without a schema behaves as it did before and omits the field.

Successful structured results survive canonical event serialization, live projection, persisted recording replay, and process/session recovery without type loss, mutation, or dependence on workstation artifacts.

A downstream workstation can render .Inputs[n].StructuredResult, including nested fields and arrays, and attempting to use an absent structured result fails prompt construction with a clear diagnostic rather than an accidental string parse.

you work list --json and relevant you work watch lines expose structuredResult as a native JSON value, human-readable Work list output uses deterministic compact JSON, and older records without a result remain readable.

Malformed JSON and schema-invalid JSON produce terminal structured_output_schema_violation dispatch failures with safe actionable detail, no propagated structured result, and configured onFailure routing; invalid schema configuration is rejected as a workstation misconfiguration.

Focused unit, projection/replay, contract, CLI, and functional tests directly prove storage/replay, downstream prompt rendering, Work observability, backward compatibility, and typed schema-violation routing, and generated interfaces remain synchronized.

Typecheck passes; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green; focused and required broader tests pass.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared/generated-file contention are resolved against current origin/main, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Preserve a validated structured result on Work
userStories.description: As a factory author, I want a schema-valid worker response stored as typed Work data so later behavior does not depend on reparsing raw text or files.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a workstation whose outputSchema is a valid JSON Schema, a conforming object, array, scalar, boolean, or null final response is decoded once and returned from worker execution as detached native JSON in structuredResult while existing raw output remains available for diagnostics and compatibility.

The successful dispatch event records structuredResult, resulting Work receives the value, and live projection, persisted recording replay, and recovery reproduce the same JSON types and value; multiple resulting Work items receive independent equivalent values.
Workstations without outputSchema do not require JSON and omit structuredResult from events and Work projections, including replay of older events that lack the field.
Invalid JSON Schema configuration is rejected deterministically as a typed workstation misconfiguration before a worker response can be accepted.
Authored public contracts, generated outputs, handwritten mappings, and clone paths preserve the optional native JSON value and ownership boundaries.
Focused worker-execution, event serialization, projection, replay, and recovery tests pass.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Render upstream structured results in downstream prompts
userStories.description: As a factory author, I want downstream workstation prompts to access an upstream JSON result directly so I can build reliable multi-stage factories without artifact-parsing handoffs.
acceptanceCriteria: A downstream prompt can access the complete upstream value at .Inputs[n].StructuredResult and render nested object fields and array elements with supported Go-template expressions.

The prompt-template contract advertises .Inputs[n].StructuredResult as optional for each available input, and runtime prompt construction returns a clear diagnostic when a template attempts to use a missing result; it does not substitute raw output, payload, an empty object, or artifact content.
Structured values supplied to prompt rendering are detached from canonical Work state so template execution cannot mutate the stored result.

A functional test built through root.BuildProcess and Process.Execute, using an allowed provider command-runner edge mock and deterministic synchronization, proves an upstream schema-valid response is stored and its nested value appears in the actual downstream provider prompt.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented detached structured-result prompt rendering, optional prompt-contract metadata and absence diagnostics, plus root BuildProcess/Process.Execute functional coverage for nested objects and arrays.

userStories.title: Route schema violations as typed dispatch failures
userStories.description: As a factory operator, I want invalid structured worker output to fail explicitly and follow factory failure routing so corrupt data never reaches a later stage.
acceptanceCriteria: Malformed JSON and valid JSON that violates outputSchema complete the dispatch as failed with stable reason structured_output_schema_violation and terminal non-retryable normalized failure policy.

Failure detail contains an actionable customer-safe validation summary with instance or schema location when available, never reports an empty error, and does not copy the complete rejected payload into the message or logs.

The rejected value is absent from resulting Work, downstream prompt inputs, success, continue, and rejection outputs, and structured-result projections; configured onFailure Work is emitted through existing routing semantics.
The typed reason survives dispatch event serialization, recording replay, Factory Session and Work projections, and public failure mapping without transport reclassification.

A functional test built through root.BuildProcess and Process.Execute, using an allowed provider command-runner edge mock and no sleep-based synchronization, proves schema-invalid output reaches the configured failure state or route, exposes structured_output_schema_violation, and causes no success-stage dispatch.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Added terminal structured_output_schema_violation classification for malformed/schema-invalid output, safe validation diagnostics, onFailure routing, generated public enum/mappings, replay/session projection coverage, and root-built functional coverage proving no success-stage dispatch. Review follow-up now builds bounded instance/schema/keyword diagnostics without rejected values or host paths, with scalar pattern coverage at focused and functional boundaries; the pkg-boundary count is restored to the main baseline.

userStories.title: Inspect structured results through Work commands
userStories.description: As a factory operator, I want Work list and watch output to show validated results so I can monitor stage handoffs without opening artifacts or decoding escaped JSON.
acceptanceCriteria: you work list --json represents structuredResult as a native optional JSON value on each Work result, not an escaped string, and list/get transport contracts and mappings preserve the same shape.
you work watch includes structuredResult on the transition line where canonical Work first has the value and omits it from unrelated transitions, failures, unstructured Work, and older recordings.

Human-readable Work list output renders deterministic compact JSON for objects, arrays, scalars, booleans, and null; you work watch preserves one complete JSON object per line, and large values follow existing bounded-output conventions.
Focused CLI and contract tests exercise structured and unstructured Work, JSON type preservation, watch line framing and order, omission semantics, and replay-backed output.

Public workstation and Work command documentation explains outputSchema, .Inputs[n].StructuredResult, typed violation behavior, and list/watch visibility with an end-to-end example that has no artifact handoff.
Generated public interfaces are regenerated from authored sources after rebasing, and generated conflicts are resolved by regeneration rather than manual merging.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Replaced the customer-representable watch null sentinel with raw event-payload presence handling. Reducer application restores only fields whose canonical raw value is JSON null, preserving the exact historical sentinel string as a string while keeping explicit null and omission distinct. Added focused decode/reducer/render coverage for both values; Work/CLI/functional suites, contract/docs checks, typecheck, test, vet, and repository quality gates pass. Review follow-up moved the recorded Work identity and structured-result projection helpers into the existing invocation-output owner so the transitioner stays within the backend-size and maintainability limits without changing behavior.
